paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. David had a dream in his heart, and God said no. David didn't sulk and he didn't quit. He stood up in front of the whole nation and pointed to what God HAD done, and then he put everything he had into helping Solomon build what he never would (1 Chronicles 28:2-6). I think that's one of the hardest things to do, and it's one of the most beautiful.

Notice what David hands his son. He gives him a call, plans and a warning: "know the God of your father and serve Him wholeheartedly and with a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands the intent of every thought" (1 Chronicles 28:9). God cares about the heart behind the work, not just the work. And the door stays open, because "If you seek Him, He will be found by you" (1 Chronicles 28:9). That's the kind of God we're baking for, friend.

Then David says it twice: "Be strong and do it" (1 Chronicles 28:10), and later, "Be strong and courageous, and do it." He gives the reason right there: "for the LORD God, my God, is with you" (1 Chronicles 28:20). Solomon's courage doesn't come from Solomon being tough. It comes from God being near. So whatever job God has put in front of you, baker, you don't have to be the biggest or the bravest, because you won't be doing it alone.
